श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता:
*
[ अध्याय ७
मतलब यह है कि संसार मेरेसे पैदा हो जाता है, पर मैं | जैसे कोई कह दे कि ये अपने सब-के-सब शरीर पार्थिव
मिटता नहीं हूँ, जैसा-का - तैसा ही रहता हूँ ।
सोना, मिट्टी और लोहेके दृष्टान्तमें गहनोंमें सोना दीखता
है, बर्तनोंमें मिट्टी दीखती है और अस्त्र-शस्त्रोंमें लोहा
दीखता है, पर संसारमें परमात्मा दीखते नहीं । अगर बीजका
दृष्टान्त लें तो वृक्षमें बीज नहीं दीखता । जब वृक्षमें बीज
आता है, तब पता लगता है कि इस वृक्षमें ऐसा बीज है,
(पृथ्वीसे पैदा होनेवाले) हैं, इसलिये इनमें मिट्टीकी
प्रधानता है तो दूसरा कहेगा कि ये मिट्टी कैसे हैं ?
मिट्टीसे तो हाथ धोते हैं, मिट्टी तो रेता होती है; अत:
ये शरीर मिट्टी नहीं हैं । इस तरह शरीर मिट्टी होता हुआ
भी उसको मिट्टी नहीं दीखता । परन्तु यह जितना संसार
दीखता है, इसको जलाकर राख कर दिया जाय तो अन्तमें
जिससे यह वृक्ष पैदा हुआ है । सम्पूर्ण वृक्ष बीजसे ही एक मिट्टी ही हो जाता है ।
। ।
निकलता है और बीजमें ही समाप्त हो जाता है । वृक्षका
आरम्भ बीजसे होता है और अन्त भी बीजमें ही होता
है अर्थात् वह वृक्ष चाहे सौ वर्षोंतक रहे, पर उसकी
अन्तिम परिणति बीजमें ही होगी, बीजके सिवाय और
क्या होगा? ऐसे ही भगवान् संसारके बीज हैं अर्थात्
भगवान् से ही संसार उत्पन्न होता है और भगवान्‌में ही लीन
हो जाता है। अन्तमें एक भगवान् ही बाकी रहते हैं—
'शिष्यते शेषसंज्ञः ' ( श्रीमद्भा० १० । ३ । २५)।
वृक्ष दीखते हुए भी 'यह बीज ही है ' - ऐसा जो जानते
हैं, वे वृक्षको ठीक-ठीक जानते हैं और जो बीजको न
देखकर केवल वृक्षको देखते हैं, वे वृक्षके तत्त्वको नहीं
जानते। भगवान् यहाँ ‘बीजं मां सर्वभूतानाम्' कहकर
सबको यह ज्ञान कराते हैं कि तुम्हारेको जितना यह संसार
दीखता है, इसके पहले मैं ही था, मैं एक ही प्रजारूपसे
बहुत रूपोंमें प्रकट हुआ हूँ - ' बहु स्यां प्रजायेय'
(छान्दोग्य० ६ । २ । ३) और इनके समाप्त होनेपर मैं ही
रह जाता हूँ। तात्पर्य है कि पहले मैं ही था और पीछे
मैं ही रहता हूँ तो बीचमें भी मैं ही हूँ ।
|
।
विचार करें कि इन शरीरोंके मूलमें क्या है ? माँ- बापमें
जो रज - वीर्यरूप अंश होता है, जिससे शरीर बनता है,
वह अंश अन्नसे पैदा होता है। अन्न मिट्टीसे पैदा होता
है । अतः ये शरीर मिट्टीसे ही पैदा होते हैं और अन्तमें
मिट्टीमें ही लीन हो जाते हैं । अन्तमें शरीरकी तीन गतियाँ
होती हैं- चाहे जमीनमें गाड़ दिया जाय, चाहे जला दिया
जाय और चाहे पशु-पक्षी खा जायँ । तीनों ही उपायोंसे वह
अन्तमें मिट्टी हो जाता है । इस तरह पहले और आखिर में
मिट्टी होनेसे बीचमें भी शरीर या संसार मिट्टी ही है ।
परन्तु बीचमें यह शरीर या संसार देखनेमें मिट्टी नहीं
दीखता । विचार करनेसे ही मिट्टी दीखता है, आँखोंसे
नहीं । इसी तरह यह संसार विचार करनेसे परमात्मस्वरूप
दीखता है । विचार करें तो जब भगवान् ने यह संसार रचा
तो कहींसे कोई सामान नहीं मँगवाया, जिससे संसारको
बनाया हो और बनानेवाला भी दूसरा नहीं हुआ है । भगवान्
आप ही संसारको बनानेवाले हैं और आप ही संसार
बन गये । शरीरोंकी रचना करके आप ही उनमें प्रविष्ट
हो गये - 'तत्सृष्ट्वा तदेवानुप्राविशत्' ( तैत्तिरीयोपनिषद्
२ । ६) । इन शरीरोंमें जीवरूपसे भी वे ही परमात्मा हैं ।
| अतः यह संसार भी परमात्माका स्वरूप ही है ।
यह संसार पांचभौतिक भी उन्हींको दीखता है, जो
विचार करते हैं, नहीं तो यह पांचभौतिक भी नहीं दीखता ।
परिशिष्ट भाव—अपनेको सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंका बीज कहनेका तात्पर्य यह है कि सब प्राणियोंके रूपमें मैं ही हूँ ।
सृष्टि अनन्त है । अनन्त ब्रह्माण्डोंमें अनन्त जीव हैं । परन्तु उन अनन्त जीवोंका बीज (परमात्मा ) एक ही है । अनन्त
सृष्टि पैदा होनेपर भी उस बीजमें कोई फर्क नहीं पड़ता; क्योंकि वह अव्यय है - ' बीजमव्ययम्' ( गीता ९ । १८ ) ।
उस एक ही बीजसे अनेक प्रकारकी सृष्टि उत्पन्न होती है (गीता - दसवें अध्यायका उनतालीसवाँ श्लोक) । बीजको
कितनी ही सूक्ष्म दृष्टिसे देखें, उसमें फल-फूल - पत्ते आदि नहीं दीखेंगे; क्योंकि वे उस बीजमें कारणरूपसे विद्यमान
हैं । उस बीजसे पैदा होनेवाले वृक्षके दो पत्ते भी आपसमें नहीं मिलते - यह अनेकता भी उस एक बीजमें ही रहती
है।
सृष्टिकी एक-एक वस्तुमें अनेक भेद हैं। विभिन्न देशोंमें मनुष्योंकी अनेक जातियाँ हैं । उनमें भी इतना भेद है कि दो
मनुष्योंके अँगूठेकी रेखाएँ भी परस्पर नहीं मिलतीं । उनके रूप, स्वभाव, रुचि, प्रकृति, मान्यता, भाव आदि भी परस्पर
नहीं मिलते। गाय, भैंस, भेंड़, बकरी, घोड़ा, ऊँट, कुत्ता आदिकी अनेक जातियाँ हैं और उनकी एक-एक जातिमें भी अनेक
भेद हैं। वृक्षोंमें भी एक-एक वृक्षकी अनेक जातियाँ होती हैं। एक-एक विद्याको देखें तो उसमें इतने भेद हैं कि उनका
english:
Here's the translation of the given Hindi text into English:

The meaning is that the world is born from me, but I am like someone who says that all these bodies are not destroyed, just like - as is, so is. 

Like the example of gold, clay, and iron, gold is seen in ornaments, clay is seen in vessels, and iron is seen in weapons, but the Supreme Being is not seen in the world. If we take the example of a seed, the seed is not seen in the tree. When the seed comes into the tree, then it is known that this tree has such a seed, (earth-born) beings are like this, so they say that these bodies are made of clay, but another will say, how can these bodies be made of clay? Clay is washed with hands, clay is sand, so these bodies are not made of clay. In this way, the body is made of clay, but it does not seem to be clay. But this world, as much as it is seen, if it is burned to ashes, then ultimately it is known that from which seed this tree has been born. The entire tree is reduced to a seed and a seed, and ultimately it is reduced to a seed. 

The beginning of the tree is from the seed, and the end is also in the seed, that is, that tree, whether it lives for a hundred years, its ultimate transformation will be in the seed, what else will be? Similarly, God is the seed of the world, that is, the world is born from God, and ultimately it is merged in God. Ultimately, only one God remains - 'शिष्यते शेषसंज्ञः' (Shrimad Bhagavat 10.3.25).

Those who know that this seed is the tree, they know the tree perfectly, and those who do not see the seed and only see the tree, they do not know the essence of the tree. God says here, 'बीजं मां सर्वभूतानाम्' (Bijam Maam Sarvabhuutanam), that is, you all know that this world, as much as it is seen, its previous existence was me, I have manifested in many forms - 'बहु स्यां प्रजायेय' (Chandogya 6.2.3), and when these are destroyed, I remain. The meaning is that I was before and I will remain after, so I am in the middle also.

Think about what is the root of these bodies? The part of the mother and father, which is the seed, from which the body is formed, that seed is born from food. Food is born from clay. So, these bodies are born from clay and ultimately merge in clay. The three states of the body are - whether it is buried in the ground, whether it is burned, or whether it is eaten by animals and birds, in all three ways, it ultimately becomes clay. In this way, in the beginning and end, it is clay, so in the middle also, the body or the world is clay. But in the middle, the body or the world does not seem to be clay. It is seen with thought, not with the eyes. In the same way, this world is seen as the Supreme Being with thought. Think about it, when God created this world, He did not take anything from anywhere to create it, and the creator is not another. God Himself created the world and became the world. By creating bodies, God Himself entered them - 'तत्सृष्ट्वा तदेवानुप्राविशत्' (Taittiriya Upanishad 2.6).

In these bodies, the Supreme Being Himself is the living being. So, this world is also the form of the Supreme Being. This world is seen as five elements by those who think, not by those who do not think. 

Appendix - The meaning of saying that I am the seed of all living beings is that I am in all living beings in all forms.

The creation is infinite. In infinite universes, there are infinite living beings. But the seed (Supreme Being) of all these living beings is one. The seed does not change even when infinite creation is born. That seed is avyaya - 'बीजमव्ययम्' (Gita 9.18). From that one seed, various kinds of creation are born (Gita 10.41). 

However, no matter how much we see the seed with a subtle vision, we will not see fruits, flowers, leaves, etc. in it, because they are present in the seed as causes. The two leaves of the tree born from that seed do not meet each other - this diversity is also present in that one seed.

There are many differences in each and every thing in creation. There are many castes of humans in different countries. Even in the same caste, there are so many differences that the fingerprints of two humans do not match. Their forms, nature, habits, nature, beliefs, emotions, etc. also do not match. There are many castes of animals like cows, buffaloes, goats, sheep, horses, donkeys, dogs, etc. and in each caste, there are many differences. There are many castes of trees. In each and every branch of knowledge, there are so many differences that their branches do not meet each other.
